name: overflow
title: Diagnostic: layout overflow
summary: Deliberately flawed: a banner forced to 400 dp (requiredWidthIn [400, 400]) inside a 300×200 document with no scroll container, so it runs past the right edge and the audit reports layout_overflow naming it.
prompt: A 300×200 card with a banner forced to 400 dp wide, not in a scroll container.
teaches: Recognise layout_overflow: a child forced wider than its parent (requiredWidthIn [400, 400]) is laid out past the document edge and clipped
Fix it by letting the child fill the parent (fillMaxWidth), or by putting it in a horizontalScroll container

snippets.note: the flaw: a required 400 dp width in a 260 dp slot

check.describe: audit reports exactly one finding, layout_overflow, whose example is the BoxLayout at x 20, w 400 (the Java reference layout also gives 400); the render shows the banner cut at the right edge. Resized, the padded box fills the window; the 400 dp banner still overflows at 200 wide and only fits once the document is 440 dp or wider.

pitfalls: A plain width: 400, or widthIn [400, 400], does not overflow in the Java reference or the TypeScript player: both clamp the size to the parent's constraints (as Compose does), so the banner silently becomes 260 wide. Only requiredWidthIn (DimensionConstraints) overrides the parent; the C++ player lets widthIn overflow too, which is a player difference, not the reference behaviour
